facts.raw_span: an 8-month history of a growing, painful tumor on her right buttock
denied experiencing fevers, chills, sweats, weight loss, or malaise
chronic kidney disease
genital herpes simplex virus (HSV)
no history of genital warts, HIV, or inflammatory bowel disease
a 5 × 7-cm verrucous, exophytic tumor with scant yellow drainage on the right medial buttock extending to the perianal skin
Superficial bacterial cultures were obtained from the lesion and grew methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
Microbial cultures were negative for deep fungal infection and acid-fast bacteria
positive for HSV type 2
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showing hyperplastic epidermis with ulceration, necrosis, and dense inflammatory infiltrate
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showing plasma cells and focal multinucleated keratinocytes with gray-blue cytoplasm
Positive staining for herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2 within epithelial cells, including multinucleated keratinocytes

concepts.why: The patient has a history of genital herpes simplex virus and the microbial cultures and immunohistochemistry results are positive for HSV type 2.
The physical examination and histology results show a verrucous, exophytic tumor with hyperplastic epidermis, ulceration, and dense inflammatory infiltrate, consistent with verrucous carcinoma.
The superficial bacterial cultures grew methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, indicating a MRSA infection.

rationales.F06: The presence of a verrucous, exophytic tumor is a strong indicator for C02.
rationales.F07: The growth of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in superficial bacterial cultures is a strong indicator for C03.
rationales.F09: The positive result for HSV type 2 is a strong indicator for C01.
rationales.F12: The positive staining for herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2 is a strong indicator for C01.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's 8-month history of a growing, painful tumor and the physical examination findings of a 5 × 7-cm verrucous, exophytic tumor are more specific to Verrucous carcinoma, although the presence of HSV suggests a possible co-infection.
